# Ledger: shop-web prod 20260412-0915

Mode: Fast (the operator asked for it; the incident is already over, which would otherwise default to Deep)
Budget used (final, after wave 3): 20 / 20 data queries (8 CloudWatch get-metric-data calls, 1 S3 fetch, 11 sqlq; 28 free control-plane reads logged, not counted) · 0 GB Logs Insights scanned / 2 · 38 / 100 CloudWatch metric requests · S3 module: 65.4 MB charged (est. $0.0070), 24h total 2011.0 / 2048 MB

## Problem

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| What | Reporter: "a spike of 403s on shop.example.com yesterday afternoon … I want to know what was being blocked and whether real customers were affected." Measurable restatement: WAF `BlockedRequests` on web ACL `example-shop-acl` (default Block response = HTTP 403) rose from ~20-30 per 5 minutes to ~1,180-1,200 per 5 minutes; which rule, which paths/clients, and whether any blocked client was a real customer. |
| Where | shop-web, prod, account 111122223333, us-east-1; web ACL `example-shop-acl` (REGIONAL) on ALB `shop-web-alb`; no siblings (one ACL, one ALB). |
| When | Reported: starts around 13:40 UTC on 2026-04-11, lasts a bit over an hour (reporter's words, explicit zone UTC). True onset: see Windows and Timeline (rule-level 60 s data, W2-Q1). |
| Who is affected | At intake unknown (the question). After wave 3: mostly a 62-client automated-looking group (97.4% of the 19,186 blocks, W3-Q3, W3-Q6..Q11); at most one browser-shaped client outside the group was rate-limited (>= 111 blocks, Likely); no sign of broad customer impact (Likely). |
| Trigger | A chat request from the operator; no alarm (W0-Q12: no CloudWatch alarm exists), no ticket. |
| Mitigations already applied | none known |
| Assumptions made at intake | (1) The window used the explicit zone in the request (13:40 UTC), taken as given: incident 2026-04-11 13:40-14:50 UTC = 13:40 + "a bit over an hour". (2) The operator's report-display zone is UTC (answered in chat when asked; `environment.md` has no `timezone`); so local time equals UTC in the report. (3) Fast mode chosen on the operator's request. (4) "Yesterday" = 2026-04-11 because the fixture clock reads 2026-04-12 09:15:30 UTC. (5) Service name `shop-web` and env `prod` taken from the request and environment.md. (6) The default Block action has no custom response configured (get-web-acl shows `Block: {}`), so the WAF's own answer is HTTP 403. |

## Impact

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Symptom | WAF rule `rate-limit-coupon` (rate-based: 10 requests per 300 s per IP on URI paths starting `/api/cart/coupon`) blocked ~1,160-1,200 requests per 5 minutes (about 230-250 per minute) for roughly 87 minutes; the default Block response is HTTP 403. |
| Affected | prod, web ACL `example-shop-acl` in front of `shop-web-alb`; the path is inside the cart core flow (`/api/cart`). In 13:40-14:50 UTC the rule blocked 15,552 requests, all rules 15,808, against 48,465 allowed: 24.6% of what the ACL saw (baseline 0.65% the hour before and a week earlier). AllowedRequests did not fall (+4% against both baselines). Who the blocked clients were is NOT known yet. Customer-facing. |
| Since / ongoing | 13:42 UTC on 2026-04-11 (W2-Q1, W3-Q13; first seen between 13:40 and 13:45 on 5-minute data, W1-Q1); ongoing: no, the last rule block is at 15:09 UTC (W2-Q1), 87 minutes later. |
| Suggested severity | After wave 1: SEV2 (provisional). After wave 3: SEV3 (suggested; the incident owner decides) because the 24.6% block share was containment of an automated group on one core-flow path, with at most one possibly real client rate-limited and about 2,119 group requests let through; SEV4 if that client is a script and no coupon request succeeded. |
| Basis | WAF CloudWatch metrics against the previous window and -7d: W1-Q1, W1-Q2, W1-Q3 · label: Confirmed for the counts, Assumed for who was blocked. The ALB-side metrics (W1-Q4..Q6) returned no data. |
| Third party in the path | none |

## Hypotheses

| ID | Statement | Expected if true | Falsification query | Model | Label |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Real customers were blocked: shoppers sharing egress addresses (carrier/corporate NAT, VPN) or a client that retries coupon calls tripped `rate-limit-coupon` (limit 10 per 5 min per IP), so legitimate coupon/cart requests got 403. | Many blocked addresses, each moderately above the limit; ordinary browser user agents and header shapes; session client keys present; blocked clients also have allowed cart/checkout requests; TLS fingerprints of normal browsers. | sqlq `clients`, `user_agents`, `header_shape`, `client_keys`, `fingerprints`, `asns`, `countries` on the fetched onset slice (W3-Q6..Q12): blocked traffic concentrated in a few networks with a single user agent, sparse headers, no client keys, one TLS fingerprint refutes it. | main | Ruled out |
| H2 | Automated abuse (coupon-code guessing, credential-stuffing style bot fleet) against `/api/cart/coupon`, correctly blocked by the rate-limit rule. | Many addresses, same user agent and sparse header-name list, few or no client keys, one or few TLS fingerprints, only the coupon path, ramp-up as the fleet starts. | the same W3 queries: broad normal user agents and header shapes with client keys on the blocked requests refute it. | main | Likely |
| H3 | A WAF configuration change (rule created, limit lowered, or COUNT switched to BLOCK) made the rule start blocking traffic that was already there. | A wafv2 write event shortly before 13:42 and again before 15:09 (to explain the stop); zero earlier blocks by that rule; the rule absent from earlier metric history. | CloudTrail wafv2 write events 11:40-15:25 and `UpdateWebACL`/`CreateWebACL` over the 14 days before (W2-Q2, W2-Q3, W2-Q4); none near 13:42 or 15:09 refutes it. | main | Ruled out |
| H4 | An application or client release (new front end, retry loop on the coupon call) started at ~13:42 and caused ordinary users to hit the limit. | A shop-web deploy (ECS service update or new task definition) or merged change within ±15 minutes of 13:42; legitimate user agents. | CloudTrail ECS `UpdateService` near the onset and `gh` commits/runs (W2-Q5, W2-Q6, W2-Q7); no deploy near 13:42 refutes it; also refuted if the blocked traffic is not browser traffic (W3-Q6, W3-Q9, W3-Q10). | main | Ruled out |
| H5 | Another rule moved: the IP-reputation or geo rule caused the 403 spike. | `BlockedRequests` of those rules rising at 13:40. | rule metrics at baseline refute it (W1-Q1 against W1-Q2/W1-Q3). | main | Ruled out |

- H1 status: refuted (as the cause of the spike) · evidence: W3-Q4, W3-Q5 (98.0% of all blocks are one rule on one path), W3-Q6 (python-requests 18,488 of the blocks; the four browser UAs are blocked 0.74%, 479 of 64,846), W3-Q7 (top-50 clients: one /24, 89.8% blocked, 0 client keys), W3-Q8 (cookie-holding top-50 clients: 9 blocks in 2,451 requests), W3-Q9, W3-Q10, W3-Q11 (62 clients: one header shape, one JA4, one ASN, 0 client keys) · note: residual, not refuted: at least 1 client outside the group was rate-limited at least 111 times (arithmetic, Likely); real customer or script is Assumed. Falsification query shown: the same sqlq set.
- H2 status: supported · evidence: W3-Q5 (all rate-limit blocks on POST /api/cart/coupon), W3-Q6 (python-requests/2.31.0 and one odd UA), W3-Q9 (5-header shape, no cookie, no accept-language, no referer), W3-Q10 (one JA4, 62 clients, 0 client keys), W3-Q11 (one ASN), W3-Q12 (four countries), W3-Q13 (ramp 13:42-13:47, plateau, decay to 15:09) · note: Likely, not Confirmed: automation is inferred from client-reported and fingerprint fields; no origin-side or load-balancer record shows what the requests did (coupon-guessing intent is Assumed).
- H3 status: refuted · evidence: W2-Q2, W2-Q3, W2-Q4 (all empty), W2-Q1 (decay over 10 minutes, not a step back) · note: falsification queries shown in the Query log; CloudTrail lookup covers management events only. The rule being silent before 13:42 (W1-Q7) is therefore "never reached 10 requests from one address in 5 minutes", not "newly created" - but the 7.5-day metric coverage is not explained by a creation event (no CreateWebACL in 14 days), see Gaps.
- H4 status: refuted as the source of the blocked traffic · evidence: W3-Q6, W3-Q9, W3-Q10 (the blocked requests are 97.4% from one non-browser group, not from a shop client release) plus W2-Q5 (no ECS UpdateService) · note: a deploy is NOT otherwise cleared (ECS unreadable, gh returned nothing); no old-against-new split exists, so no deploy gets any label.
- H5 status: refuted · evidence: W1-Q1 vs W1-Q2/W1-Q3: IP-reputation 175 (incident) vs 208 (previous) vs 201 (-7d); geo-block-embargo 81 vs 99 vs 106; flat. Falsification query shown: the same get-metric-data, `Rule` = `AWS-AWSManagedRulesAmazonIpReputationList` and `geo-block-embargo`.
- Not run: `from-history:` (no `incidents/` directory exists, `ls` showed only environment.md), `sched:` hypotheses (class is not `scheduled`; the schedule listings W1-Q8..Q11 returned nothing).

| No application log group found under `/ecs/` (W0-Q3 `{}`) | Application-side status of allowed requests, and any app errors, not read | Give the exact log group name(s) |
| ALB CloudWatch metrics returned no data (W1-Q4..Q6 `{}`) | Availability cross-check (app/ALB 4xx and 5xx against WAF blocks) and what the origin returned for allowed requests are not available; the 24.6% share is a WAF-side share only | Confirm the ALB dimension value (LoadBalancer=app/shop-web-alb/9f8e7d6c5b4a3210) and check the ALB metrics in the console for 13:40-15:10 UTC |
